items.title: Allen Toussaint Interview, 1979-03-13
items.q: It knew where it was during the Roy Brown days.

ctx.x: monetarily? I guess the results and more opportunities for more local artists.

As far as I'm concerned, opportunity is always there. So, I couldn't get into that part. Whether it is as strong now as it was some years ago, and not to pinpoint five, no, it's not strong now. Now, for one thing, it is ground some through a peculiar period that wasn't heyday period. New Orleans knew exactly where it was during Fats Damanoyer. It knew where it was during the Roy Brown days. We knew where we were during early Armour Thomas, Ernie Cato. You knew exactly where that whole thing was, Jesse Hills. You…

I want others on the other hand that played authentic New Orleans music a long time ago will go in and do that again. So both of those things are, they seem like misfits to me for today. The normal growth is what that would be if it would continue growing until today. But it takes a constant flow of success for people to stand that upright and last that long. Or either be very strong to come out on the other side, which I prefer. Because whether people buy you music or not, it still should grow and not be stunted…
